active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.direct on an 8-parameter C3-orbit family with a movable outer orbit
active_paradigms.description: The current program obtains its score by fixing an equilateral triangular hull, imposing 3-fold symmetry, using five differential-evolution runs in six variables, and then using COBYLA to improve ten independently movable interior points. Its important strength is that symmetry sharply reduces the difficult nonsmooth maximin search and its fixed triangular gauge makes normalized determinant constraints easy to evaluate. Its main structural limitation is that the three hull vertices are permanently locked: the only boundary orbit is forced to be exactly the equilateral vertices, which excludes C3-symmetric configurations whose outer orbit is slightly interior or whose hull is created by a different orbit. Parameterize 13 points as one center plus four rotational C3 orbits, with each orbit represented by polar radius and phase, giving eight variables; designate the largest-radius orbit as the hull orbit and evaluate the true ConvexHull-normalized objective rather than divide by a fixed triangle determinant. Make one scipy.optimize.direct call over bounded radii and phases, using a deterministic fixed geometry and enough function evaluations for an 8D partition search. Penalize orbit collisions and any radius ordering violation, but do not require all points to remain inside a predetermined triangle because the evaluator accepts any finite nondegenerate point set and normalizes by its own hull. This directly targets the missing hull-shape freedom while retaining the symmetry principle that made the current solution viable. After the offline search, hard-code the resulting coordinates so evaluation itself is effectively instantaneous.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; specifically remove the fixed-equilateral-hull restriction while preserving a low-dimensional symmetry reduction. The final static result also substantially improves eval_time over five DE runs plus COBYLA.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use the evaluator's exact absolute determinant divided by ConvexHull(points).volume, not the current fixed hull_det shortcut. Keep phases modulo 2*pi and impose a small radial separation between orbit representatives to avoid duplicate points or unstable hull changes. scipy.optimize.direct availability depends on the installed SciPy version, so retain a deterministic static fallback candidate.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.root to solve an active-triangle contact system rather than optimize a nonsmooth minimum
active_paradigms.description: The current COBYLA phase correctly recognizes that successful configurations are governed by many active triangle-area inequalities, but it only preserves the orientation signs observed at one DE incumbent and can stall when the active set changes. Convert the best known configuration into an active-set equation problem: identify the triples whose signed normalized determinants are within a tight band of the minimum and select an independent set of equations setting them equal to a common variable t. Add gauge equations fixing translation, rotation, and scale, plus stationarity equations derived from nonnegative multipliers on the selected signed determinant constraints. Solve this square KKT/contact system in one scipy.optimize.root call, initialized from a literal copy of the current best configuration and its active multipliers. This differs fundamentally from COBYLA/SLSQP-style inequality optimization: it seeks the equioscillating geometric contact point that a local maximin optimum must satisfy. Verify every one of the 286 unsigned areas after the solve, recompute the actual convex hull area, and only use the root solution if it strictly exceeds the stored incumbent. The useful offline procedure is to determine one promising independent active set from the incumbent's near-minimum triples and then bake that set, signs, and starting vector into the program. This can make small but real improvements where COBYLA stops because its trust-region linear models cannot accurately resolve a dense active manifold.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary bottleneck area through exact equalization of the limiting triangles; it is most useful for extracting the last improvement from a known high-quality oriented-matroid cell.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not include every near-active triple, since root requires a square, well-conditioned residual system; use rank-revealing QR offline to choose independent equations. The KKT multiplier signs and all nonactive inequality slacks must be validated afterward, since a root can find a saddle or a solution in a different sign cell. Preserve a hard-coded incumbent and reject nonfinite, degenerate, or lower-scoring root outputs.

active_paradigms.idea: Replace runtime optimization with a hard-coded offline-certified coordinate table using numpy.asarray
active_paradigms.description: The evaluator has no prescribed unit region and no independent containment test: any 13 finite points are scored only by the smallest of 286 triangle areas divided by the area of their own ConvexHull. Therefore affine transforms do not affect the score, and an expensive search need not occur during heilbronn_convex13 at all. Run the strongest exploration and exact verification offline, retain the single best 13-by-2 coordinate table, optionally affine-normalize it to a numerically comfortable hull, and return numpy.asarray(table, dtype=float). The present program spends nearly all evaluation time in five large differential-evolution calls and a 50,000-iteration COBYLA call, despite caching only helping if the function is invoked repeatedly in one process. A static table retains exactly the discovered score on every call and removes optimizer-version, timeout, and stochastic convergence sensitivity. To make this a genuine improvement rather than merely a speed change, use the broader four-orbit hull family or active-contact solve offline to obtain a table above the current 0.731044 combined score before embedding it. Independently calculate all 286 determinants and the SciPy ConvexHull area using the final decimal literals, because coordinate rounding can change which almost-active triangle is limiting. Include the current symmetric construction only as a static fallback if the final table somehow fails a finite-value or positive-area check.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Eval_time and deterministic reproducibility directly, while preserving or improving min_area_normalized through an offline-discovered and evaluator-verified coordinate certificate.
active_paradigms.cautions: Do not round coordinates aggressively: near-equal active constraints can lose score at 12-digit versus full double precision. Ensure the table has exactly shape (13,2), no repeated points, and a strictly positive-area hull. A static candidate is only as good as the offline evaluator used to certify it, so score it with precisely the provided formula rather than a fixed assumed hull area.

tried_paradigms.idea: Lift the 3-fold ansatz and use one full-dimensional differential-evolution search over a convex-polygon hull parameterization
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is strong because it exploits affine invariance, fixes an equilateral triangular hull, reduces the search to six 3-fold-symmetric variables, evaluates all 286 triangles exactly, and finally performs an epigraph SLSQP refinement. Its main limitation is structural: it requires exactly three prescribed hull vertices, a center point, and three rotational point orbits, so it cannot represent configurations with a non-triangular hull, broken symmetry, or uneven orbit geometry. Replace this restricted representation by a parameterization with, for example, 5--7 hull vertices described by sorted angles and positive radial values, plus interior points represented by convex combinations of that polygon's vertices. Use a single scipy.optimize.differential_evolution call on this parameterization, with a fixed seed and an objective equal to the actual minimum absolute determinant divided by the shoelace area of the parameterized hull. Canonicalize affine freedom by fixing three hull degrees of freedom, such as setting two vertices to (0,0) and (1,0) and fixing a third vertex's x-coordinate. Penalize invalid cyclic hulls, self-intersections, nearly zero hull area, and interior points outside the polygon. This directly searches oriented-matroid families unavailable to the current triangular/3-fold design and may discover that the best 13-point normalized configuration has more than three extreme points.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; specifically remove the current symmetry and triangular-hull restrictions while retaining exact evaluation of all 286 triangle areas. Runtime is controlled by a moderate population and fixed maximum generation count.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The evaluator has no unit-area or bounding-box constraint: only the ratio to ConvexHull area matters, so do not optimize raw areas or accidentally impose a scale penalty. The parameterized shoelace denominator must match the true ConvexHull area; enforce strict convex cyclic order so that it does. Differential evolution should be the only optimization call, rather than followed by a local optimizer, and its returned candidate should be rechecked with scipy.spatial.ConvexHull before caching.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a direct nonsmooth COBYLA epigraph solve with all 13 points free after affine gauge fixing
tried_paradigms.description: The current local SLSQP stage has a useful epigraph formulation, but it freezes every triple orientation from a single symmetric incumbent and fixes the first three points as the equilateral hull. That can reject a better solution if a productive move crosses an orientation-change boundary or changes which points belong to the hull. Formulate one scipy.optimize.minimize call with method='COBYLA' over all free coordinates and an epigraph variable t, after fixing three noncollinear gauge points only to eliminate translation, rotation, and scale. Use inequality constraints |det(i,j,k)| - 2*t*A_hull >= 0 for every triple, represented as two signed determinant branches only within an explicitly selected oriented-matroid cell; choose the cell from a high-quality deterministic hand-designed configuration rather than the current forced 3-fold one. Keep the hull fixed to a chosen convex m-gon by expressing all non-gauge points in polygon barycentric coordinates, so A_hull is constant and the triangle constraints are clean. COBYLA is particularly appropriate because the maximin geometry has many active inequalities and derivative estimates of abs determinants become unreliable near equioscillation. A successful result should show many triangles tightly clustered at the achieved threshold, rather than one isolated small triangle. This is a fundamentally different local strategy from the current SLSQP refinement: optimize a less constrained, non-symmetric active-set cell directly rather than using global search followed by SLSQP.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Raise the bottleneck triangle threshold t while allowing all 13 locations to break 3-fold symmetry; optimize feasibility robustness and the primary normalized score, not raw hull area.
tried_paradigms.cautions: COBYLA accepts only inequality constraints and can be sensitive to coordinate scale, so normalize the fixed hull to O(1) dimensions and set a sufficiently large maxiter/rhobeg. A fixed sign pattern is valid only while every determinant stays positive with margin; reject any final result whose actual absolute-area score is lower than its epigraph claim. The selected hull polygon must remain the actual hull, otherwise normalization in the evaluator differs from the constant denominator used in the optimization.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use SHGO to enumerate and compare low-dimensional symmetry classes instead of committing to one 3-fold orbit topology
tried_paradigms.description: The score of 0.731044 comes from a single 3-fold topology containing three hull vertices, one center, and three generic 3-point orbits. This is an excellent low-dimensional baseline, but the true best arrangement may belong to a different finite symmetry class, such as reflection symmetry with paired points, 6-fold partial symmetry, or threefold symmetry without a center point. For each candidate class, build a compact fundamental-domain parameterization that guarantees points lie in a fixed equilateral hull, and use one scipy.optimize.shgo call to maximize the exact minimum normalized triangle determinant in that class. SHGO's simplicial sampling is valuable here because it identifies distinct basins of the piecewise-smooth minimum-area landscape rather than repeatedly evolving one population toward the same basin. The most promising alternative classes for exactly 13 points are a reflection-symmetric 6+6 pair structure plus one point, and a 3-fold structure with one orbit constrained on each side but no forced centroid point. Select a single class based on deterministic preliminary geometric reasoning and make its SHGO result the constructor output; the function call itself remains deterministic. This attacks the current program's largest issue—an unverified symmetry topology—while retaining enough dimension for a global method to be credible.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary normalized minimum triangle area through discovery of a different symmetry/orbit topology; secondary objective is reproducibility because SHGO's sampling is deterministic under fixed bounds.
tried_paradigms.cautions: SHGO scales poorly with dimension, so this is appropriate only for a deliberately low-dimensional orbit parameterization, not all 26 coordinates. Its objective is nonsmooth at changes in the active triangle; use dense enough simplicial sampling and evaluate the exact absolute determinants, not a surrogate that can alter rankings. As with the existing code, ensure all generated orbit points are inside the fixed hull and independently recompute all 286 triangle areas before returning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Directly solve a fixed-combinatorics epigraph formulation with scipy.optimize.minimize using SLSQP, allowing a non-triangular hull.
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first searches only a six-parameter 3-fold-symmetric family and then uses COBYLA with three fixed equilateral hull vertices; its strength is that every area constraint is explicit and the triangle hull makes normalization constant. Its principal limitation is structural: it excludes configurations whose convex hull has four or more extreme points, and it makes the ten non-vertex points compete inside a hull shape that may not be optimal for n=13. Replace the equilateral-hull assumption by a fixed affine gauge with a selected cyclic hull combinatorics, such as 4, 5, or 6 labeled hull points, and parameterize these hull points by convex-polygon edge coordinates while keeping their shoelace area explicitly available. Use all remaining points as independent coordinates constrained to lie in that polygon through oriented half-plane inequalities. Introduce epigraph variable t and impose signed determinant inequalities det(i,j,k)*sign(i,j,k) >= 2*t*polygon_area for every triple, with signs obtained from one deterministic non-collinear seed. Call SLSQP once from a high-quality seed, maximizing t under those smooth constraints and fixed hull-order constraints. This directly optimizes the evaluator ratio while exploring a substantially larger class than the present equilateral triangle construction.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized; specifically remove the current triangular-hull and exact-3-fold-symmetry restrictions while retaining an exact epigraph objective.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The denominator must be the signed shoelace area of the declared hull, and every non-hull point must satisfy every hull half-plane inequality; otherwise ConvexHull may return a different denominator. Maintain a positive lower bound on consecutive hull edge cross-products to avoid hull-order flips. Do not use raw absolute values in the constraints: fix signs from a strictly feasible seed, because any sign flip must pass through a forbidden zero-area triangle. Verify the returned array with the evaluator’s exhaustive 286-triple computation rather than trusting SLSQP’s t value.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.milp as a deterministic hypergraph-packing search over a dense geometric candidate set.
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit the fact that, after fixing a candidate convex container polygon and forcing its vertices to be selected, a thresholded Heilbronn feasibility problem becomes a 0-1 packing problem. Generate a deterministic non-lattice candidate cloud inside a fixed unit-area polygon using several irrationally shifted triangular lattices, boundary samples, and small fixed symbolic perturbations so that accidental collinear triples are avoided. For a chosen target normalized threshold q, create one binary variable per candidate and add the inequality x_i+x_j+x_k <= 2 for every candidate triple whose area is below q times the fixed polygon area. Force the selected count to equal 13 and force designated container vertices to equal one, then use scipy.optimize.milp with a zero or dispersion-oriented linear objective. A feasible solution is an actual 13-point configuration whose every discrete triple clears q, not merely a smooth surrogate result. Use a target slightly above the current 0.02262 score, ideally near the 0.030936889 benchmark, and use the selected points directly as a deterministic constructor output. This attacks the global oriented-matroid/combinatorial part that differential evolution and a single local COBYLA basin do not systematically enumerate.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of min_area_normalized by finding a different incidence pattern and hull membership pattern; runtime is also predictable because the candidate set and solver are deterministic.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The fixed container must be the actual hull: force enough container vertices and ensure all candidates are inside it, otherwise the evaluator’s ConvexHull denominator changes. The number of triple constraints grows cubically, so begin with roughly 60-120 carefully designed candidates rather than a huge grid. A plain regular grid is poor because many triples are exactly collinear; use deterministic irrational offsets. The MILP threshold is fixed during a single solve, so choose it based on the desired score and validate feasibility; do not claim its objective itself maximizes a continuous threshold.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.least_squares as a target-feasibility solver with a smooth squared-hinge violation residual for all triangle constraints.
tried_paradigms.description: The current code maximizes a nonsmooth minimum and relies on COBYLA after its evolutionary phase; this is vulnerable to a small active set changing and has no strong least-squares pull from the many nearly active triples. Instead, choose a desired normalized target t above the incumbent and formulate a residual vector containing squared-hinge violations max(0, t*A_hull - signed_det/2) for all 286 fixed-sign triples. Add residuals for negative hull half-plane slack, degenerating hull orientation, and optionally a small centroid/scale gauge term to remove affine drift. Use a parameterization with a chosen 4-to-6 vertex convex hull and free interior coordinates, so the residual uses the corresponding shoelace hull area and is directly aligned with evaluator normalization. A single scipy.optimize.least_squares call with method='trf', robust loss='soft_l1', and stringent tolerances seeks a zero-residual certificate at that target. If it reaches effectively zero residual, return the coordinates; this is stronger evidence than a high soft-min surrogate because every triple is explicitly checked against the target. This method is fundamentally a feasibility/certificate search rather than another evolutionary maximin search, and can find narrow equal-area contact configurations where many constraints must be satisfied simultaneously.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Crossing a specified score threshold, especially the benchmark ratio of 1.0, by satisfying all 286 triangle lower bounds simultaneously rather than improving only the current worst triple.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A least-squares objective is not the evaluator objective, so accept a result only after independently computing the exact minimum area and ConvexHull area. Residual scaling matters: normalize determinant residuals by a stable reference hull area so hull-slack penalties neither dominate nor disappear. Fixed orientation signs require a seed with no near-zero triples. If a zero-residual result is not found, retain a known valid static fallback rather than returning an infeasible least-squares iterate.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace runtime evolutionary search and COBYLA with a preselected active-set solve using scipy.optimize.root
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses a 3-fold-symmetric equilateral-triangle ansatz, five expensive differential-evolution runs over six parameters, then a COBYLA epigraph refinement with the first three points fixed as hull vertices and every triangle orientation frozen. Its strength is that it directly optimizes the evaluator's determinant-to-hull-determinant ratio and enforces feasibility by barycentric coordinates. Its principal limitation is that COBYLA is solving a highly degenerate nonsmooth problem with 286 inequalities, while frozen signs prevent it from crossing into a better oriented-matroid cell. Offline, retain the best configuration, identify all triangles within a small tolerance of the bottleneck, and select a rank-21 independent active system involving the 20 movable coordinates plus threshold t. Include any active hull-boundary contacts as equations and replace redundant triangle equalities until the Jacobian is nonsingular. At evaluation time, start from hard-coded incumbent coordinates and make exactly one scipy.optimize.root call on signed_det/hull_det minus t for this fixed active set. Verify every one of the 286 absolute areas afterward and only accept the root result if it is feasible and improves the stored incumbent. This targets an equioscillating maximin vertex much more accurately than COBYLA's trust-region termination and removes the very large current runtime cost.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary min_area_normalized, with a major secondary reduction in eval_time by replacing five global searches plus COBYLA with one deterministic nonlinear system solve.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The active equations must be selected offline from a known good incumbent; blindly taking the 21 smallest triangles can create a singular or inconsistent system. Preserve determinant signs only for the explicitly selected active equations, but validate using absolute determinants afterward because a sign crossing invalidates the local cell. Hard-code a fallback coordinate table because scipy.optimize.root can fail or converge to an infeasible equality solution.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a fixed-candidate maximin formulation solved directly as a mixed-integer linear program with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: A fundamentally different way to escape the current continuous local basin is to optimize point selection rather than perturb coordinates. Fix three affine-gauge hull vertices of a unit reference triangle and construct one deterministic, nonuniform candidate set inside it: combine a triangular rational grid with hand-placed irrational offsets around the incumbent's known point locations. Create one binary variable per candidate and force the three reference vertices to be selected, with the total selected count equal to 13. For every candidate triple (i,j,k), add the linear implication t <= normalized_area(i,j,k) + M*(3-x_i-x_j-x_k), where M is safely above one and t is the maximized bottleneck. This is exact for the discrete candidate set: whenever all three candidates are selected, the corresponding triangle constrains t; otherwise the big-M term deactivates that row. Solve the single MILP once with scipy.optimize.milp, then return the 13 selected coordinates directly. Unlike the current program, this can jump across orientation cells and can deliberately choose an asymmetric configuration rather than assuming that 3-fold symmetry is optimal. Use the MILP solution itself as a source of an offline coordinate table if a static final constructor is desired.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary score through global combinatorial topology changes; it specifically addresses the current ansatz restriction and the inability of COBYLA to cross zero-area orientation boundaries.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Keep the candidate pool moderate because all candidate triples produce constraints; roughly 40–60 carefully chosen candidates is much more practical than a dense uniform grid. The three forced vertices are necessary so the hull area is fixed and the linear objective is truly the evaluator ratio. Ensure candidate points are unique, finite, and strictly inside or on the fixed triangle, and recompute the actual ConvexHull-normalized score because numerical solver tolerances can slightly violate binary or row feasibility.

tried_paradigms.idea: Embed an offline-discovered certified coordinate table and return it with numpy.asarray
tried_paradigms.description: The evaluator has no input instance and evaluates the same 13-point configuration every time, so runtime optimization is not intrinsically valuable once a superior configuration has been found. The current implementation spends nearly all evaluation time rediscovering a deterministic incumbent through differential evolution and COBYLA, even though its cache exists only within one imported process. Run exploratory searches offline only, including searches over hull combinatorics with more than three hull points and without imposed rotational symmetry, and retain the best fully validated coordinate array. Affinely normalize the selected configuration to a convenient scale, noting that the evaluator ratio is affine invariant when all points undergo the same nonsingular affine transform. In the submitted constructor, create that literal 13-by-2 double-precision table via numpy.asarray and return a copy. Before embedding, evaluate all 286 determinant areas in double precision and independently run ConvexHull to certify the exact score under evaluator arithmetic. This is structurally different from trying another runtime optimizer: it converts any expensive offline breakthrough into a deterministic O(1) constructor and eliminates optimizer variance, import-time dependency risk, and timeout exposure.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Preserve and deploy the highest offline min_area_normalized exactly, while minimizing eval_time essentially to array construction and making reproducibility absolute.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not round coordinates aggressively: the minimum is controlled by active near-equal triangles, so 8-digit decimal literals can noticeably lower the score; embed at least 16 significant digits. Do not accidentally reorder, duplicate, or post-normalize only part of the points. A table from a fixed triangular-hull search may still be inferior to an offline configuration whose ConvexHull has additional extreme points, so compare candidates using the evaluator's actual hull normalization rather than a fixed reference denominator.
